chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha' said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who manumits his slave conditionally (mudabbar), and he is in good health, then later the master needs money; is it permissible for him to sell him? He said: Yes, if he needs to that.
ai.seo_question: Can a master sell a mudabbar slave if he needs money?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the financial need (hajah) of the owner serves as a valid condition for selling the mudabbar, overriding the deferred manumission. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the status of a slave whose freedom is contingent upon the owner's death, prioritizing the owner's economic necessity. It reflects the practical application of property rights within the master-slave dynamic as understood by the Ahl al-Bayt.
